### Project Name

Agent Client Protocol (ACP)

### Project Description

The Agent Client Protocol (ACP) standardizes communication between code editors/IDEs and AI coding agents, similar to how the Language Server Protocol (LSP) standardized language server integration. It was created by Zed Industries and is co-developed with JetBrains. ACP decouples agents from editors, solving the M×N integration problem where every new agent-editor combination previously required custom work. The protocol supports both local agents (JSON-RPC over stdio) and remote agents (HTTP/WebSocket) are being implemented to align on a standard.

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

- Providing an open, interoperable protocol for connecting any AI coding agent to any editor, allowing for better distribution for new agent teams to access developers in the tooling they are already using.
- Being developed openly by multiple companies under the Apache 2.0 license
- Complementing MCP: MCP handles tool/data connectivity while ACP handles the editor-agent UX layer
- Operating transparently with public governance and RFD process

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

- MCP: ACP is complementary to MCP. MCP standardizes how AI models connect to tools, data, and applications. ACP standardizes how coding agents communicate with various clients for interaction with agent sessions. ACP re-uses MCP JSON representations where possible, and allows clients to configure MCP servers for their agents.
- goose: Block's goose agent has implemented ACP support.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

Agents natively implementing ACP: Augment Code, Cline, Cursor, Factory Droid, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Goose, Junie, Kimi CLI, Kiro CLI, Mistral Vibe, OpenCode, OpenHands, Qwen Code, and more.

Clients/Editors implementing ACP natively or through plugins: Zed, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, Emacs, Obsidian, Jupyter Notebooks, marimo notebook, and many others.

### Governance Model

The current governance documents are here: https://agentclientprotocol.com/community/governance

We modeled the core maintainer and working group structure heavily based on MCP's governance.

Key points:
- Lead Maintainers (BDFL): Ben Brandt (Zed Industries) and Sergey Ignatov (JetBrains)
- Core Maintainers: Agus Zubiaga, Anna Zhdan, Niko Matsakis
- Hierarchical structure: Contributors → Maintainers → Core Maintainers → Lead Maintainers
- Decision process: Core maintainer group meets bi-weekly; uses RFD process for proposals and Zulip for communication

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

- CI workflow (`ci.yml`): Runs on every push/PR to `main`. Checks formatting (prettier + rustfmt), typos, clippy linting, builds, tests, and verifies generated schema files are up to date.
- Release workflow (`release-plz.yml`): Automated releases via `release-plz` on merge to `main`. Creates release PRs automatically and publishes to crates.io. Uploads JSON schema files as release assets on GitHub Releases.

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

Documented at: https://agentclientprotocol.com/rfds/about

ACP uses a Request for Dialog (RFD) process for specification changes:
1. Propose by opening a PR with an RFD document
2. Champion from the core team merges to "Draft"
3. Implementation begins (feature-gated)
4. Move to "Preview" for broader community review
5. Move to "Completed" with core team sign-off

### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker

The main schema repo is at: https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/agent-client-protocol/issues

Each SDK also has their own issues as well.
